Claim 1: A method for applying aerodynamically functional film to a body around which complex flow occurs, in particular to a commercial aircraft, having the following steps:
determining the flow lines (4) on the surface (7) of the body around which flow occurs for a predetermined surrounding flow state on the basis of a computer model (1) of the body with the aid of numerical flow simulation;
developing at least one surface segment (3) of the computer model (1) provided with flow lines (4) to form a two-dimensional surface;
locating at least one coherent field (10, 20, 30, 40) in the developed surface segment (3) having local flow directions readable at the flow lines (4) in a predetermined angle range around a main flow direction of the respective field (10, 20, 30, 40); and
applying and possible trimming aerodynamically functional film to the body around which flow occurs within the field boundary (10.1-4, 11.1-4, 12.1-4, 13.1-4) of the at least one field (10, 20, 30, 40) located in the developed surface segment in such a way that the aerodynamically functional film is aligned along the main flow direction of the respective field.
Claim 2: The method as claimed in claim 1, wherein the field boundary (10.1-4, 11.1-4, 12.1-4, 13.1-4) and the alignment of the main flow direction are selected in accordance with alignment lines identifiable on the body, so that alignment and possible trimming of the aerodynamically functional film in a field (10, 20, 30, 40) take place on the basis of the correspondingly identified alignment lines on the body.
Claim 3: The method as claimed in any one of the preceding claims, characterized in that the alignment lines are identified on the basis of structural features of the surface of the body, which are also mapped in the computer model (1), and/or on the basis of a geometrically calibrated pattern projected on the body.
Claim 4: The method as claimed in any one of the preceding claims, wherein the main flow direction of a field (10, 20, 30, 40) is selected in parallel to an alignment line for a field boundary (10.1-4, 11.1-4, 12.1-4, 13.1-4) of the field (10, 20, 30, 40).
Claim 5: The method as claimed in any one of the preceding claims, characterized in that the field boundaries (10.1-4, 11.1-4, 12.1-4, 13.1-4) of at least one field (10, 20, 30, 40) on the developed surface segment are straight lines and preferably form a closed traverse having at most 8, preferably at most 6, more preferably having 4 sides.
Claim 6: The method as claimed in any one of the preceding claims, characterized in that for the possible trimming of the aerodynamically functional film, before application of the aerodynamically functional film, one or more knifeless tapes are applied along the alignment line of at least one field boundary (10.1-4, 11.1-4, 12.1-4, 13.1-4) of the field (10, 20, 30, 40) on the body.
Claim 7: The method as claimed in any one of the preceding claims, characterized in that the aerodynamically functional film is applied in at least one field (10, 20, 30, 40) in the form of film sections (8) like tiles.
Claim 8: The method as claimed in any one of the preceding claims, characterized in that the predetermined angle range is ±70 or less, preferably ±5° or less, more preferably ±30 or less.
Claim 9: The method as claimed in any one of the preceding claims, wherein at least two, preferably adjoining fields (10, 20, 30, 40) are located in the surface segment (3).
Claim 10: The method as claimed in any one of the preceding claims, wherein sufficiently many fields (10, 20, 30, 40) are located that the predetermined surface segment (3) is completely filled with fields (10, 20, 30, 40).
